  "text": "The loose pages listed repairs to the quay: timber bought, stones hauled, wages paid to men whose names Mara recognized from old gravestones. Daniel turned each sheet by its dry corners while she followed the dates with her finger.

Near the bottom of one page, a line had been crossed out so heavily that the paper was nearly torn.

“Can you read it?” she asked.

Daniel held it toward the fire. “Something about a gate. North gate, perhaps.”

Their father came over with the poker still in his hand. He looked at the line, then at the drawing on the table. “There used to be steps at the north end of the quay. They were covered when the new warehouse went up.”

Mara remembered the warehouse wall, damp and green at its base. On the drawing, a short passage ended beneath a square marked with a faint X.

“Could that be it?” she asked.

“It might be.” Their father set down the poker. “We’ll show the harbor master in the morning.”

Daniel looked disappointed, but the window had already gone black. Their father moved the ledger farther from the hearth, where it could dry without scorching, and sent them upstairs.

Mara lay awake listening to the last drips from the roof. Once, she heard someone walking along the lane, their footsteps slow on the wet stones. By the time she reached the window, the lane was empty. Across the harbor, a lantern burned beside the quay."
